description: Union all consecutive vertices in bounded half-open ranges using DSU component right boundaries to skip already-merged intervals.

source.title: RangeUnionFind
source.author: Nyaan
source.license: CC0 1.0; algorithm description only, clean-room implementation
source.algorithm_attribution: Each component stores its leftmost vertex and exclusive right boundary. Range union repeatedly merges the component containing a with the component beginning at the current right boundary until that boundary reaches b.

operations.0: unite all consecutive vertices of [a,b); require 0<=a<=b<=n; return current component count
operations.1: return whether a and b are connected; require 0<=a,b<n
operations.2: return component size of a; require 0<=a<n and b=0

contract.range_semantics: The vertices are a,a+1,...,b-1; added adjacency edges are (i,i+1) for a<=i<b-1.
contract.right_boundary_invariant: Every component is a contiguous vertex interval. right[root] is its exclusive right endpoint; find(a)'s right endpoint identifies the next component boundary to merge.
contract.empty_or_single_vertex_range: No-op; return the unchanged component count.
contract.tie_rule: Union by size; representative choice is unobservable.
contract.maximum_result_argument: Each of 32 operations returns at most 32; the one-based weights sum to 528, so the loose checksum ceiling is 16,896.

workspace.meaning: Three fixed 32-element signed 64-bit arrays for DSU parent/size and component left/right boundaries; implementations with narrower arrays use less.

complexity.primary_time: O((n+q)*alpha(n)) amortized; each adjacency boundary is merged at most once
complexity.independent_oracle_time: O(q*(n+E)) for explicit adjacency storage and BFS, with E<=n-1
